clue.text: Hedonistic request for guaranteed soliciting

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
sure means certain, guaranteed
soliciting means asking for, seeking

explanation.surface: Someone describes a self-indulgent appeal for a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, so a hedonistic person is always chasing enjoyment.

clue.text: Make actor sing in part, playing for time

indicators.note: make here means fashion or form, so the following letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A director tells an actor to sing in one part of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is the anagram signal: the fifteen letters of ACTOR SING IN PART are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaying action to gain time is exactly what putting things off amounts to.

clue.text: Voices to measure up on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to time something is to measure its duration

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take stock on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for measure; in a down clue it is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to utter or give it out, a sense of the verb emit.

clue.text: Wandering one-star politician in the US

indicators.note: wandering means straying from place to place, so these letters move out of order

explanation.surface: A low-ranked officer drifts aimlessly through American politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' rearranges the letters of ONE-STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of the US Senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Name Cod Mornay given today

indicators.note: cod as an adjective means fake or mock, so the next word is a sham version of itself, its letters rearranged

parts.note: to day: D, the abbreviation for day, is added on

explanation.surface: A menu announces the fish dish on offer today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like the fish but is the anagram signal: MORNAY becomes RAYMON, and 'given today' adds D for day.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond is a man's first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Actress Sarah did wrong with children around!

indicators.note: around means the word for children encloses the other piece

parts.note: sons are male children

indicators.note: done wrong, these letters come out in a different order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a famous actress misbehaved in front of her kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DID, and 'around' has the children enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Siddons was the most celebrated English tragic actress of the late eighteenth century.

clue.text: Permit for headless chicken in need of a name

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the word for chicken is cut off

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
a title is the name of a book or work

explanation.surface: A headless chicken running about needs a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes H from HEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them the right to do something, to authorise or allow it.

clue.text: I'm on to it: aborigine has no leader like Rory Bremner

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

indicators.note: has no leader means the first letter of the word for aborigine is dropped

parts.note: an aborigine is a native of a land

explanation.surface: Someone spots an Aboriginal impressionist lacking a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no leader' takes N from NATIVE, leaving ATIVE. Rory Bremner is a British TV impressionist.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist mimics others, so his style is copying or mimicking.

clue.text: Parting gift makes favourite worker tremble

parts.note: a golden boy or girl is a favourite
a hand is a manual worker
to shake is to tremble

explanation.surface: A leaving present makes the boss's pet employee quake.
explanation.definitionFit: A large payment given to an executive on leaving a company is a lavish farewell present.

clue.text: Weepy old head getting stared at

parts.note: onion is old slang for the head, as in off one's onion
eyed means looked hard at

explanation.surface: An elderly headmaster finds himself the focus of everyone's gaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a headteacher, but it is the slang onion for one's head; 'off one's onion' is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes watering as if from cutting an onion are tearful, given to weeping.

clue.text: A case of a pain in the neck

definitions.meaning: a case in a court of law is heard before a judge
an annoying person or thing is a burden to be endured

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a court hearing and an affliction that tests one's patience.

clue.text: King turned to Emperor for Italian dish

indicators.note: turned means the word for King is reversed

parts.note: sir, like sire, is a courtly form of address to a king
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: A monarch defects to an emperor's side to get some Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes SIR into RIS; 'to' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a creamy rice dish from northern Italy.

clue.text: Profound indignation shown by our generation about time

indicators.note: about means the words for our generation go round the letter for time

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: Our generation is deeply angry about the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the phrase for our generation wrap the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is fierce anger at something shocking, a deep sense of indignation.

clue.text: Pigeon travels to and fro

indicators.note: a word that travels both ways reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A pigeon flies back and forth on its rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the answer itself, which reads the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The nun is a breed of fancy pigeon, named for its hood-like crest.

clue.text: Fundraiser in the name of God turning sweet

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembled piece is read backwards
in means the fundraiser is placed inside the Latin word for God

parts.note: Deus is the Latin name of God
a rag is a British student charity fundraising event

explanation.surface: A charity event in God's name turns sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the fundraiser inside Deus and 'turning' reverses the result. A rag week is British student charity fundraising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sugared has been sweetened with sugar, so it is sweet.

clue.text: Garden pot broken by sponsor

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden pot gets smashed by someone backing the project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges GARDEN POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Swallow meat, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter of meat is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is told to swallow meat, though not straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' drops M from MEAT; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to eat it.

clue.text: To marry is hard when following second language

indicators.note: following means the rest comes after the letter for second

parts.note: to wed is to marry
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Getting married is tough when it comes after learning a second language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' means the rest comes after S, standing for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedish is the language of Sweden.

clue.text: We without love and misery

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word goes round the other letter

parts.note: O, the zero score in tennis, is called love

explanation.surface: Being without love leaves us in misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so WE wraps O.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is great sorrow or distress, a synonym for misery.

clue.text: It's thorough in Department H

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Office gossip about the thorough work done in Department H.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study covers a subject comprehensively and in detail.

clue.text: Stalk founder of the Met, holding up detectives

indicators.note: holding means the founder's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel founded London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: The man who founded London's police force keeps detectives waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CID into DIC and 'holding' puts it in PEEL. The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicel is the small stalk bearing a single flower.

clue.text: Attack a la Thatcher the worker getting the sack

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: Thatcher's style of attack sees a worker fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the sack' suggests dismissal, but the sack is just a bag. Margaret Thatcher was famed for berating ministers, swinging her handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: To handbag is to attack verbally and ruthlessly, a verb coined from Margaret Thatcher's style.

clue.text: Stand roughly centre-left

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters are only loosely in order

parts.note: centre spelt out plus L, the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A politician takes a roughly centre-left stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges CENTRE plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a reading stand for a book or notes.

clue.text: Leonard is upset by film with Simone Signoret

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Leonard is distressed by a French film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges LEONARD.
explanation.definitionFit: La Ronde is Max Ophuls's 1950 French film, in which Simone Signoret starred.

clue.text: Follower in company with Tom gets round piano

indicators.note: gets round means the abbreviation for company encircles the letter

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A fan keeps company with Tom as they circle the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Coy, the army abbreviation for a company, is unusual; 'gets round' has it encircle the piano letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat imitates others, following their lead slavishly.

clue.text: Ms Gardner started an avalanche

indicators.note: started means the letters are taken from the start of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star triggered an avalanche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' takes the opening letters of AVALANCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava Gardner was an American film star of the 1940s and 1950s.

clue.text: Magic lamp holder has a line to tack on at home

parts.note: to add is to tack on
in means at home

explanation.surface: The owner of a magic lamp gets an extra line to attach at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin is the folktale hero who owns the lamp with a genie in it.

clue.text: Traveller found with curious cask and bundles again

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters of the word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A salesman discovers an odd barrel and parcels it up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges CASK as ACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack goods is to bundle them up once more.

clue.text: Rise of Conservative member

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP is going up in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean ascend or move upward, as a road or a price does.

clue.text: Alice cured of the small intestine

indicators.note: cured means treated or processed, so the letters of the name are reworked

explanation.surface: A girl called Alice has been treated for a bowel complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' rearranges ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac relates to the ileum, the last part of the small intestine.

clue.text: Porcelain for bishop given to a friend

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a means one
china is rhyming slang: china plate means mate

explanation.surface: A gift of fine china for the bishop goes to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: China for mate comes from Cockney rhyming slang, china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine porcelain made with bone ash.

clue.text: Joked about TV programme, one with leaves

indicators.note: about means the word for joked goes round the other piece

parts.note: gagged means told gags, joked
tele is short for television
a table is a schedule or programme, as in timetable

explanation.surface: Someone cracked jokes about a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the word for joked wrap the TV word. 'Leaves' suggests a plant, but they are the hinged flaps of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateleg table has hinged flaps, called leaves, supported by swinging legs.
